title: Health Equity Through Breast Cancer Patient Data

title: Health Equity Through Breast Cancer Patient Data
text:
Overview
Access to timely care is not evenly distributed in the United States. This project, completed for Bayesian Statistics at Macalester College, asks which factors affect whether a breast cancer patient is diagnosed within 90 days of their first hospital visit, among patients diagnosed between 2015 and 2018.

title: Health Equity Through Breast Cancer Patient Data
text:
Approach

Combined patient-level breast cancer data with zip-code demographics and state-level hospital data
Explored differences in timely diagnosis by state, race, insurance type, income, and age
Fit Bayesian logistic regression models, including a ridge-style regularized model, and checked convergence and fit with trace plots, autocorrelation, and posterior predictive checks

title: Health Equity Through Breast Cancer Patient Data
text:
Key Findings

Where a patient lived was strongly associated with timely diagnosis. Holding personal and zip-code demographics constant, a patient in Minnesota had roughly nine times the odds of a diagnosis within 90 days as a similar patient in Alabama.
Insurance type also mattered, with commercially insured patients making up the largest share of timely diagnoses.
Limitations include having only a yes/no outcome rather than days to diagnosis, and no hospital-level data.

title: The Impact of the ACA on Healthcare Access in Minnesota
text:
Overview
The Affordable Care Act expanded health insurance coverage across the country, but its effects were not the same everywhere. This project, completed for the Projects in Data Science capstone at Macalester College, examines how healthcare access and health outcomes changed across Minnesota’s counties before and after the ACA.

title: The Impact of the ACA on Healthcare Access in Minnesota
text:
Approach

Combined Census Small Area Health Insurance Estimates (SAHIE) with County Health Rankings data from 2010 onward
Compared before-and-after trends in insurance coverage and county health indicators, including clinical care, health behaviors, and the physical environment
Contrasted the state’s largest counties with its smallest to see whether county size shaped the ACA’s impact
Built an interactive R Shiny app with county-level maps that lets users explore coverage trends by year, age, sex, and income

title: The Impact of the ACA on Healthcare Access in Minnesota
text:
Key Findings

Uninsured rates fell sharply across Minnesota after the ACA took effect.
Large counties saw significantly greater improvement in health indicators than small counties.
The uninsured rate ticked back up slightly between 2015 and 2019, a period of rising premiums and reduced federal support for the law.

title: Tonight, Sorted
text:
Overview
Tonight, Sorted is a recommender app for figuring out what to do. You describe a plan the way you’d text a friend, such as “four of us want something fun and social tonight, not too expensive,” and the app returns three real places near you, each with a short explanation of why it fits.
Built as the final project for Analytics for Unstructured Data in the UT Austin MSBA program, it brings together free-text understanding, embeddings, retrieval, and live data from several APIs.

title: Tonight, Sorted
text:
How It Works
A planner LLM reads the request and decides which specialist agents it actually needs, then adapts if a step comes back empty. The app shows its work, including which agents ran or were skipped and how every venue was scored.








Step
What it does
Method




Preference
Turns free text into group size, budget, likes, dislikes, and hard vs. soft constraints
LLM with structured JSON output


Discovery
Ranks 196 activity ideas by meaning, not keywords
Sentence embeddings and cosine similarity


Local places
Finds real venues near the user
Google Places API


Weather, events, travel
Scores outdoor suitability, finds live events, and estimates drive times with traffic
Open-Meteo, Ticketmaster, Google Routes


Website evidence
Reads each venue’s website and reviews and judges fit only from retrieved passages
Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)


Matching
Produces the final ranking
Weighted score across activity fit, venue quality, travel, and evidence


Synthesizer
Writes the plain-language explanation
LLM, with code verifying it kept the ranking

title: Tonight, Sorted
text:
Design Principle
LLMs interpret and explain, while Python does all of the arithmetic. When a signal is missing, such as a venue with no website, it is dropped and the remaining weights are re-normalized instead of being filled with a made-up value. This keeps the rankings transparent and reproducible.

title: The Reality of Home Field Advantage
text:
Overview
Home field advantage is one of the most debated ideas in baseball. Fans, crowds, batting last, and familiarity with a park’s quirks are all thought to help the home team, but how much do they really matter, and does the effect differ from team to team?
This project, completed for the Causal Inference capstone at Macalester College, estimates the causal effect of playing at home on winning for every MLB team, using game data from Retrosheet and Baseball Reference.

title: The Reality of Home Field Advantage
text:
Approach

Built a causal graph (DAG) to map how home field could affect winning through factors like attendance, comfort, and performance, and to identify confounders such as opponent strength, starting pitcher, day or night games, and day of the week
Used partial exact matching to compare home games against similar away games for each team
Estimated the average treatment effect on the treated (ATT) and on the controls (ATC) for all 30 teams
Ran E-value sensitivity analyses to test how strong an unmeasured confounder would need to be to explain away the results




Causal graph used to guide the analysis

title: The Reality of Home Field Advantage
text:
Key Findings

About half of the league showed a statistically significant boost in win rate at home.
Teams with distinctive ballparks, such as the Colorado Rockies, Toronto Blue Jays, and New York Yankees, showed some of the largest effects, consistent with factors like elevation and park design.
Some teams, including the Cincinnati Reds and Chicago Cubs, showed no significant home field advantage.




Estimated effect of playing at home on win rate for each team, with confidence intervals





How many games each team would have won in 2023 without home field advantage
